content: FSTL1, also known as Follistatin-related protein 1, is a protein encoded by the FSTL1 gene in humans. This protein shares structural similarities with follistatin, a known BMP-4-binding protein. FSTL1 specifically binds to BMP-4 and TGF-β1 but does not interact with Activin A. Its structure includes an FS module, which is a follistatin-like sequence containing 10 conserved cysteine residues. Additionally, it contains a Kazal-type serine protease inhibitor domain, two EF-hand domains, and a Von Willebrand factor type C domain. FSTL1 plays a significant role in various developmental processes, including the development of the lungs, ureters, central nervous system, and skeletal system. In the context of rheumatoid arthritis, FSTL1 is thought to act as an autoantigen. It upregulates proinflammatory mediators that are critical in the pathogenesis of arthritis. Furthermore, serum levels of FSTL1 have been found to correlate with the severity of arthritis, suggesting its potential as a biomarker for disease progression. FSTL1 also appears to have a cardioprotective role. It has been shown to mitigate cardiac hypertrophy following pressure overload and to prevent myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury in animal models, such as mice and pigs. Muscle-derived FSTL1 is involved in modulating vascular remodeling in response to injury. Moreover, FSTL1 has demonstrated a remarkable ability to stimulate cardiac regeneration following myocardial infarction, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic agent in cardiovascular diseases.
